Power Platform · Identity & Governance

Block the Power Apps Maker Portal with Conditional Access

Restrict app creation and editing without preventing people from running published apps. · September 2026

The one thing to remember: target the maker portal as its own Microsoft Entra cloud application. Do not block the Power Apps player application if users still need to run published apps.

What this control does

Microsoft Entra Conditional Access evaluates access when a token is issued. The Power Apps maker portal and the Power Apps player are separate first-party applications, so a policy that blocks make.powerapps.com can stop targeted users from building while leaving app playback available.

ExperienceApplication IDExpected result
Maker portal
make.powerapps.com		a8f7a65c-f5ba-4859-b2d6-df772c264e9dBlocked for users in the policy
Power Apps player
apps.powerapps.com		9362bc14-3e81-4ef9-8b77-f1c40afe68e0Unaffected by this policy
Scope check: this page covers tenant sign-in control with Conditional Access. Power Platform's separate environment app access control governs which client applications can reach Dataverse in a managed environment. Use that feature when your requirement is environment-level data protection, not simply blocking the maker portal.

Before you start

  • Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2.
  • Global Administrator or Conditional Access Administrator permissions.
  • A pilot group and at least two emergency access accounts excluded from the policy.
  • A plan for who retains maker access, such as platform administrators or an approved maker group.

Configure the policy

1

Make the maker portal selectable.

In the Entra admin center, open Identity → Applications → Enterprise applications and search for make.powerapps.com. Microsoft documents the application ID above. If the first-party service principal is not present in your tenant, provision it once with Microsoft Graph PowerShell:

Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Applications -Scope CurrentUser
Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "Application.ReadWrite.All"
$appId = "a8f7a65c-f5ba-4859-b2d6-df772c264e9d"
$sp = Get-MgServicePrincipal -Filter "appId eq '$appId'"
if (-not $sp) { New-MgServicePrincipal -AppId $appId }
2

Create a report-only policy.

Go to Protection → Conditional Access → Policies → New policy. Include the pilot users or a controlled group first. Exclude emergency access accounts, Power Platform administrators, and anyone who must retain maker access. Under Target resources, select Cloud apps and choose make.powerapps.com. Under Grant, choose Block access. Set Enable policy to Report-only.

3

Test both paths.

Have a pilot user open the maker portal and a published app. In Identity → Monitoring & health → Sign-in logs, filter by the maker portal and confirm the report-only result indicates it would be blocked. Confirm the player sign-in succeeds.

4

Turn the policy on.

After the pilot behaves as expected, change Enable policy to On and save. Roll out by group if you need a staged adoption path.

What users should experience

Blocked

Maker access

Targeted users cannot access make.powerapps.com and receive a Conditional Access access-blocked message.

Allowed

App playback

Users can still open published apps from apps.powerapps.com, direct links, Teams, or an embedded experience, subject to the app's own permissions.

Operational safeguards

  • Protect emergency access. Keep at least two break-glass accounts excluded and monitor their use.
  • Use named locations carefully. If makers should work only from trusted networks, add a location condition that excludes approved named locations from the block.
  • Pair controls by layer. Conditional Access governs who can sign in to the portal. Environment security groups, DLP policies, Managed Environments, Dataverse roles, and environment app access control govern what users and client apps can do after that.
  • Expect propagation time. Microsoft notes that Power Platform app access control changes can take up to an hour to take effect. Validate sign-in and audit evidence before treating a change as complete.

Troubleshooting

SymptomLikely causeNext check
Maker portal is missing from the pickerThe service principal is not provisioned or the wrong app was selected.Verify the documented maker portal application ID and the Enterprise application.
Policy is not appliedThe user is excluded, the policy is still report-only, or another assignment does not match.Review policy evaluation details in the sign-in log.
Published apps are also blockedThe policy targets the player application or a broader resource than intended.Target only make.powerapps.com and test the player application separately.
Dataverse access is denied for a client appEnvironment app access control is blocking the client application.Review the environment's app access mode, allow/block list, and audit events.
